name: Cache key per account/source/location/user/role
summary: Key = account + source + snapshot location + user + role, plus a noactivity suffix when ACTIVITY=0; another location, user or role never gets this copy

name: Memory 24 h, file CACHE_HOURS
summary: Memory (checked first without the lock) then file then read under the key's lock; store() keeps memory, file and SQL copy; drop() under the lock; memory only inside Snowflake; Snowflake reads themselves also kept as parts (business_rule:read_parts)

name: Findings keep only the last run
summary: SP_ACCESS_FINDINGS deletes every TBL_ACCESS_FINDING row before appending, in one transaction

name: Local versions listen on HOST only
summary: run.py streamlit passes --server.address HOST (default 127.0.0.1); .streamlit/config.toml binds 127.0.0.1 for a plain streamlit run

name: Read parts keep case-only duplicate columns
summary: DuckDB column names ignore case, so write_part tags a column whose name differs from an earlier one only in case as <name>#dup<n> (SHOW's name next to ACCOUNT_USAGE's NAME); read_part drops the tag again, so the row keeps both keys (cache.py:397, 410-416, 434).

name: One snapshot run at a time
summary: Insert the RUNNING row first, then only the earliest RUNNING run of the last hour goes on; others delete their row and return SKIPPED

name: Snapshot data tables keep no Time Travel
summary: TBL_ACCESS_ data tables are created with DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 0 and the RETENTION_* (may fail) statements set it on existing tables: each run deletes older runs' rows, so Time Travel would only store copies

name: Activity tab counts
summary: activity(name, what, user): queries per day over ACTIVITY_DAYS ending at the snapshot day for an object, user, role, app (APP) or scope (OBJECT_NAME under name + '.'), totals by user/role/client/statement/object split into read/write/ddl, one row per user+role+client+object+statement+action with hours per UTC hour (weekdays), weekend and weekend_hours, first_day, kind and interactive; counts are per action, so a MERGE that reads and changes a table counts twice.

name: Activity hours in UTC, business time as an offset
summary: activity_sql groups per UTC day and keeps HOURS = {UTC hour: queries} (access.py:1703-1704, 1723-1729); activity() splits them into weekday hours and weekend_hours (access.py:6132-6137); the UI counts off-hours as weekend queries plus weekday hours outside [start, end) after shifting by a UTC offset (offOf, web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:25-26); default start-end from WORK_HOURS 7-19 (access.py:119, server.py:3018)

name: Activity view by object type
summary: activity_page picks the view from the object's kind: STREAMLIT -> app (rows where APP = name), DATABASE / SCHEMA -> scope (every object under the name), WAREHOUSE -> who ran queries on it from the usage read (warehouse_use, no ACCESS_HISTORY), else object; app and scope get no grant-path graph; as=<user> keeps one user's use for an object, app or scope view (the object page's Access for) (server.py:3008); the graph takes focus= (server.py:3029)

name: ACTIVITY=0 reads no ACCESS_HISTORY
summary: ACTIVITY=0: snapshot() reads no OBJECT_USE / ACTIVITY table, live() probes neither ACCESS_HISTORY nor SESSIONS (access.py:1287-1288), SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT skips both steps; sources SKIPPED, note 'skipped (ACTIVITY=0)', rules 24-28 skipped (skipped_rules), the Activity tabs and Granted vs used say so (server.note_info, server.py:593-596); its own cache key (_noactivity)

name: Copy-only SQL behind the Activity tab
summary: query_sql(name, what, first, last): read-only SELECT over ACCESS_HISTORY x QUERY_HISTORY x SESSIONS listing every query id, time, user, role, statement, object and client in the window (no query text), filter per what (object, user, role, app by StreamlitName, scope by LIKE prefix), quotes doubled; the app never runs it

name: App's own queries left out of activity
summary: The app's own queries are left out of the activity. Both names are settings: QUERY_TAG (env, default 'access-explorer', access.py:107) is set on the app's connection (sf.py:35); STREAMLIT_APP (env, default ST_ACCESS_EXPLORER, read into APP_ST, access.py:108) is the app inside Snowflake. activity_sql and ACT_BASE drop QUERY_HISTORY rows with that tag, rows whose StreamlitName is that app, and the TBL_ACCESS_ tables SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT writes (access.py:1720-1726, 6243-6244); quotes and backslashes are escaped first (access.py:1697, quoted() at 4493). The procedure takes both from !define QUERY_TAG / STREAMLIT_APP (sql/1_setup.sql:210-211, 1057-1063); local .env, sis/.env and settings.local.sql must agree.

name: SQL behind each Activity section
summary: One query per Activity section over ACCESS_HISTORY x QUERY_HISTORY x SESSIONS for the name and window, default business hours, TZ_HOURS=0; sent as section_sql. See logic/page-sql.md.

name: Grant path behind a use
summary: used_path(user, role, object, action): user -> shortest chain to the role used -> shortest data_use chain to a holder of a privilege that fits the action (READ_PRIVS for READ, else WRITE_PRIVS or OWNERSHIP) -> object; None when the role reaches no such grant now (admin role, grant gone).

name: Activity read window (incremental)
summary: Window = ACTIVITY_DAYS (60) back from now, cut at UTC midnight (TIMESTAMP_TZ literal, not the session time zone); rows of an earlier read are kept up to the day before its last day, and that day onwards is read again (ACCESS_HISTORY lags up to 3 hours). Same in SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT activity() (sql/1_setup.sql:1078-1086).

name: Links granted to admin roles are dropped
summary: Hide every-role-to-SYSADMIN hierarchy

name: Admin paths capped per admin role and on the Object banner
summary: admin_paths: per admin role at most MAX_PATHS paths, shortest first (one shared cap would let SYSADMIN paths hide ACCOUNTADMIN); admin_holders: at most MAX_PATHS per grantee and admin role (access.py:3148-3158); Object page banner lists the first MAX_ADMIN_PATHS (20) user admin paths, admin_users and admin_total count all (server.py:2392, 2392, 2462).

name: Admin roles and account privileges shown red
summary: Admin holders with paths (per admin role its own MAX_PATHS cap, shortest first); ACCOUNT grants class admin

name: Streamlit app runs with its owner's rights
summary: app_exposure(app): owner = roles with OWNERSHIP on the app; sensitive = what the owner reads that is sensitive (columns, [] = whole object); holders = roles with USAGE on the app -> users reaching them; exposed = per user the sensitive objects they cannot read through their own roles (PUBLIC included); None without an owner

name: Can they?: every privilege of the type can be asked
summary: The Can they? privilege choices are valid_privs (from the data and the standard ones) first, then every other privilege Snowflake documents for the type (SNOWFLAKE_PRIVS; a schema also every CREATE <type>), so one nobody holds can be asked and answers No (access.py:4200-4240, server.py:2655). valid_privs, the matrix and the rules do not use SNOWFLAKE_PRIVS.

name: A refresh runs in the background; old data stays until the new is built
summary: Rebuild snapshot / Read Snowflake again: one JOB at a time, read under KEY + ".new" with its own parts (kept for an hour after a failure, so the next refresh resumes), timed-out reads keep the old data, built, then cache.swap and compared(d) (What changed made while the replaced data is still built, business_rule:changes_at_refresh); a failure keeps the old data and the message in JOB; locally in a thread (BACKGROUND), inside Snowflake inline (app.py); the React indicator stops and says so when the server restarted during it

name: Shortest path by BFS
summary: Shortest chain to every role

name: Can they? blocked: one line per fact and per grant
summary: A blocked answer shows the privileges held, USAGE held or missing per container, then one line per grant of the smallest fix (iac split at "; Add ") and the SQL one GRANT per line; text only (web/src/pages/Check.tsx:369-388).

name: Snowflake built-ins hidden
summary: Built-in grants left out unless builtin=1; one fold box under PUBLIC

name: One read per cache key at a time
summary: lock(key): an RLock per key (LOCKS, guarded by LOCK), so a read of one key never waits on another (shared and My access load side by side); SQL_LOCK serialises the one .cache/access.duckdb writer; drop() keeps the memory copy in OLD for last()

name: What changed is compared at refresh, while the replaced data is still built
summary: renew() swaps the new read in, then compared(d): only when cache.prev(KEY) exists and its shared_key is still in a.built does it build d and run diff_of(prev) under LOCK; else (a same-run refresh kept an older previous) the first open of What changed compares. A failure is said in the load log only. diff_of keeps one diff per data-set pair (a.cached) and, in Snowflake mode with a local cache, .cache/<key>.diff.pkl stamped (prev key, loaded key, builtin, rules_stamp, SERVER_STAMP) (server.py:3208-3227); a.diff(prev, prev_findings(prev), key, pairs=False) reuses the kept findings and built set (access.py:7066-7080).

name: Choke points / where to cut
summary: Links used by every path, fewest users losing first

name: Compare: make B equal to A
summary: match gives B what only A has, trim takes away what only B has (the first link of B's path, or its own grant; never PUBLIC; one change each), so match + trim make B equal to A; the page offers it as plan=equal, next to match (grants only) and extras (A's); the revokes can go to What if (access.py:5666-5690, web/src/pages/Compare.tsx:71-87). Text only. A path's first link is the cut, so B's other ways to the same object are not cut.

name: Grant and user events
summary: Events per grant added/removed, user status, findings

name: Same rule+grantee = same finding
summary: New / fixed findings ignore detail changes

summary: duck() builds role links, start roles and path counts per hop in an in-memory DuckDB once per data set; lose_all() answers who loses access for every fix edge in one query, read_shares() pre-counts what each role reaches; equal to the Python walk (test_duck_reach); without duckdb, with a role loop or past MAX_HOPS the Python walk runs

name: What changed events name only their first people and objects
summary: a.diff: an event lists its first EVENT_NAMES (200) people and objects (sorted, nsmallest) with capped=True when cut; impact counts all (access.py:7100-7111). changes_page sends each event's first NAMES (20) people, objects and subjects plus subject=, and with subject= and a capped event adds 'Big changes name only their first 200 people and objects, so some about <subject> may be missing here' (server.py:3165, 3187-3188, 3193-3194).

name: Graph focus: who has access to the focused box
summary: focus_access(o): for a focused database, schema or object, the people per access level as the Object page's Who tab counts them (a.who_has, cached per object), most powerful level first, plus the role count; None for a role or a box. Sent as focus.access in the graph (server.py:729-740, 989).

name: Graph focus keeps the way in through folded boxes
summary: After the walk, a kept node with incoming lines but none from a kept node (a holder fed only through a summary fold's own line) gets its upstream back from the drawn lines, so the person stays linked to the focus (server.py:846-855).

name: Graph focus: only the lines through one box
summary: build_graph focus=<box> runs narrow() before anything folds (server.py:877-884). A combined box opens into its members; a member of a combined box opens it with only that member on; a summary fold whose own lines do not reach its members stays one box; a box not drawn gives the whole graph and a note (server.py:813-827). through() keeps the focus and every node on a line through it, up and down (server.py:777-792); other combined boxes keep only members on those lines and relabel their count (server.py:835-845); cut() drops empty lanes (server.py:795-798). Over MAX_BOX objects in more than one schema the objects box again per DB.SCHEMA (scope_key; server.py:801-804, 859-863). Show all drops focus=.

summary: object -> schema -> database / type grouping

name: Summary folding over 30 boxes / 6 lanes
summary: Granted roles -> fold box -> holders -> groups

name: HIERARCHY=0 skips the rules that walk role paths
summary: HIERARCHY=0: the checks in WALKS (3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 14, 17-24, 29) do not run, rule 6 runs without its reader count, rule_rows counts no 'who loses access'; skipped_rules() lists them as 'skipped (HIERARCHY=0)', so Risks & fixes and Home show them as skipped, not passing (server.py:3496-3536, Risks.tsx:86-90); pages still walk

name: Home cards and Needs attention
summary: home_summary, once per data set: findings per severity and rule, distinct people and roles per severity, unmasked sensitive columns (rule 6), dormant readers (rule 7), and act_first: Critical then High rules, rarest first, at most ACT_FIRST (5), each with its first NAMES subjects (server.py:1897-1934). home_cards: admin holders per admin role, stale people by status, users by status and type, roles by kind, objects by type (TOP_TYPES 6 + Other), chain depth, biggest schemas and databases (TOP_BIG 6), daily queries of the last DAYS (60), object activity (90 days), and What changed counts only when that diff is already made (Home never compares) (server.py:1934-1990).

name: Can they? inside a database or schema
summary: inside_access(name, user, scope, mode): every table and view (is_data) in the database or schema, with what name holds and whether it is enough for mode read (SELECT), dml (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, as far as valid for the kind) or ddl (OWNERSHIP); OWNERSHIP or an admin role's real links give everything; without USAGE on its database and schema the row is blocked. Rows that cannot first, then by name; create = CREATE privileges held on the schema itself (access.py:5037-5067). inside_page filters show_in= all | can | cannot and in_q=, pages by INSIDE_PAGE and counts can / cannot / blocked (server.py:2775-2786).

name: Object inventory: per kind the first level that answers
summary: inventory_sql lists 20 kinds (databases, schemata, tables and views, functions, procedures, stages, pipes, sequences, file formats, streams, tasks, tags, masking and row access policies, integrations, compute pools, Streamlit apps, notebooks, alerts, warehouses) with an ACCOUNT_USAGE view, an INFORMATION_SCHEMA view and SHOW ... IN ACCOUNT where they exist (access.py:991-1057; masking and row access policies are separate entries). inventory_read: ACCOUNT_USAGE (DELETED IS NULL) per kind, else INFORMATION_SCHEMA once per standard database (not when the database list came from SHOW; a refused database skips only itself), else SHOW (temporary tables dropped; Iceberg, hybrid and materialized kinds from show_kind). The note names the kinds no level read and the kinds read with a fallback, first 20 each (access.py:1134-1185, 1128-1131). Same text in SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT (sql/1_setup.sql:718-913).

name: Ungranted objects become OWNERSHIP rows
summary: inventory_seen: per object name (before '(') its kind and whether a grant row already owns it (access.py:1060-1068). inventory_rows: for each inventory object whose ownership the grant read lacks, one OWNERSHIP row named DB.SCHEMA.NAME (unquoted); an object already granted keeps its kind; owner = the role, a database role as DB.ROLE, None when no role owns it (an application) or the read does not say (access.py:1071-1092). Direct mode appends them to GRANT (access.py:1644-1654); SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT objects() writes them to TBL_ACCESS_GRANT (IS_FUTURE and GRANT_OPTION false, GRANTED_BY NULL, GRANTEE_ROLE NULL for no owner; sql/1_setup.sql:949-966). tidy() moves an OWNERSHIP row without a grantee to d['UNOWNED'] (access.py:1991-1992, 2010); build() lists those as objects with no holder (access.py:1872-1874); the DuckDB copy writes them back into TBL_ACCESS_GRANT (cache.py:260). My access reads only the kinds with no ACCOUNT_USAGE view (Streamlit, notebooks, alerts, warehouses) by SHOW, kept when one of the user's roles owns them (access.py:903-916).

name: KEEP_BUILT built data sets
summary: Switching views restores instead of rebuilding

name: Rule results kept across restarts
summary: Shared data in Snowflake mode: findings, rows, ro, breaks saved in .cache/<key>.rules.pkl with (build key, builtin, a.rules_stamp(), SERVER_STAMP); reused while the data, the settings access.py reads, access.py and server.py are unchanged; built() works out all four in the load and saves them (server.py:208-215)

name: Crowded lanes fold into one box
summary: fold_lanes: a lane with more than MAX_LANE (24) free roles becomes box lane:<i>, more than 24 people (users or stacked boxes, counted by size) lane:<i>:people; the start, the selected box and the focus never fold, objects never; lines to members end at the box with the member count (server.py:743-774). It runs in a big (lazy) graph and in any graph with a lane over MAX_LANE (server.py:888-889). Same idea as graphs.ts foldRoles on the client.

name: Big graphs send combined boxes empty
summary: build_graph: with src (gsrc params) and more than LAZY (300) members over all combined boxes and lane boxes, the graph is big: boxes go out with counts only (lazy, a folded lane's role names in ids) and src; graph?of=<page>&group=<box> (only=) answers one box with up to MAX_MEMBERS (1000) members (server.py:886-889, 956-978, 4013-4025).

name: Database and schema lists: ACCOUNT_USAGE, then INFORMATION_SCHEMA, then SHOW
summary: database_list: ACCOUNT_USAGE.DATABASES (lags up to 3 h), else INFORMATION_SCHEMA.DATABASES from the first of up to 5 home databases that answers (the current one, granted ones, SNOWFLAKE; access.py:1366-1374), else SHOW DATABASES, else UNAVAILABLE with every reason (access.py:1105-1125). schema_list: only standard databases (no shares or applications, access.py:1101-1102); ACCOUNT_USAGE.SCHEMATA, else INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA per database (skipped when the database list came from SHOW), else SHOW SCHEMAS IN DATABASE; a database this role cannot see (unseen: 'does not exist or not authorized') is left out without a note (access.py:1188-1220, 1095-1098). The schema list feeds SHOW FUTURE GRANTS (access.py:1438-1463). Read once per load and shared by database roles, future grants and the inventory; the procedure keeps it per run in DBS, and P_SOURCE = SHOW skips ACCOUNT_USAGE (sql/1_setup.sql:224, 370-377, 832-947).

name: Loss net of other paths
summary: A user loses access only when every path is cut

name: A lost session or no warehouse stops the load
summary: lost(e): ConnectionError, OperationalError / InterfaceError, errno 606 (no warehouse: every SELECT fails, SHOW still works) or 390111/390112/390114 (to verify). live() and mine() raise it after the probe wave instead of running SHOW fallbacks (access.py:1279-1281, 856-858); a lost part is never kept (cache.py:482-483); the server answers 503 shared_unreadable / mine_unreadable with load_error(), which adds 'Set SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE in .env' for 000606 (server.py:239, 238-241, 304).

name: Map objects roll up per database
summary: map_graph: combine_tab(at=last lane) turns an objects lane over MAX_BOX (= MAX_OBJECTS, 12) into one box per database 'DB · N objects' (drill into the database); account-level objects and a database with one object stay single (server.py:1074-1104); once per data set (map_combined); params carry of=map so lazy boxes open through graph?of=map&group=; map?node=<id> answers one box's detail (server.py:2938-2940).

name: MAX_PATHS lazy listing
summary: At most MAX_PATHS chains listed, shortest always kept

name: Missing, NULL or unreadable data gives empty results plus a note
summary: tidy() fills missing columns, empties missing tables (SOURCES UNAVAILABLE), leaves out rows without names / day / action (missing_names) and notes missing snapshot columns (missing_columns); snapshot() and live() turn unreadable tables and refused SHOWs into notes; only a lost session (lost()) stops a load; note_info explains each key

name: Can they? No: the narrowest grant
summary: narrowest(name, user, priv, obj): among the roles name already reaches that hold USAGE on obj's schema (else its database) and may be suggested, the one with the fewest grant rows (then by name) gets priv on obj, so nothing else comes with it; returns the role, how many users hold it and the GRANT text (never run); None without a container or a fitting role (access.py:5292-5304). check_object asks it only on the Ways in tab (near=1), not for My access and not for OWNERSHIP (server.py:2729-2733).

name: Sub-sections live in the left nav
summary: Tabs with nav (level 1 or 2) publish themselves to the app; the side menu nests them under the open page (up to three levels) and the page hides its own bar on wide screens with the menu open (.ae-tabs-nav, .ae-wide-hide); on narrow screens or with the menu shut the bar shows (web/src/components/parts.tsx:58-70, web/src/App.tsx:197-228, web/src/App.tsx:431-435, web/src/app.css:67-68).

name: No OK snapshot run: empty pages that say so, never kept
summary: snapshot(): no OK run, no RUN_ID, or TBL_ACCESS_RUN unreadable -> every table empty with NOTES no_run; cache.store keeps such a read in memory only (no .pkl, no SQL copy) and keep_prev never sets it aside as the previous snapshot

name: Object activity: last use bucket per object
summary: object_activity() over tables and views, warehouses, Streamlit apps and procedures / functions / tasks: per object last read, last write, days since, bucket, new, use per window and history (access.py:6668-6778). History per type: warehouses DAYS_USAGE when the usage read worked, Streamlit apps ACTIVITY_DAYS when activity is readable, procedures / functions / tasks 0 (NO_USE), the rest USE_DAYS when object use is readable (access.py:6751-6752, 6660). bucket(d): <= 30 days '30', <= 90 '90', <= USE_DAYS '180', else 'none'; no history: 'nodata' (older use unknown, never 'not used') (access.py:6659, 6664-6665, 6756-6764). BASE objects count as read; a warehouse's use is its queries, an app's the queries it ran for its viewers (access.py:6727-6738). Windows PERIODS (30, 90, 180) are cumulative read / write queries and distinct readers / writers (access.py:6066, 6742-6748, 6765). new: DDL on it in the activity window (access.py:6733-6735).

name: Object activity: read-only and write-only tables
summary: pattern(window) = both | read_only | write_only | none from read and write queries; only writable kinds (no views, no external tables) with history get one; objects with no use at all add to none (access.py:6782-6789, 6768-6773). The Object activity page: days= 30 / 90 / 180 only (else 400), scope= keeps one database or schema, tabs unused (history >= days and no use or last use older than days), read_only, write_only, all (server.py:3090-3122). The Home card uses the 90-day counts (server.py:1979-1984).

name: Object use read incrementally by week
summary: use_start: window USE_DAYS back in whole ISO weeks; an earlier read's weeks are kept but its last two, which are read again (ACCESS_HISTORY lags up to 3 hours), so a refresh reads one or two weeks and gives the rows of a full read; SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT object_use does the same in SQL (test_sql.test_object_use_weeks)

name: A page never waits behind a load
summary: load_shared takes LOAD without blocking for a page: busy -> 409 shared_loading; the React app makes the page inert and polls /api/progress until the load ends, then asks again; built() already did the first page's work (rule 17, breaks, sens, server.py:211-217), and a page still waiting shows Waiting (Loading… with its seconds, after 10 s a still-working hint)

name: Which SQL a page shows to run yourself
summary: Per page and params, the read-only ACCOUNT_USAGE queries behind it with SET lines filled in (grants from access_queries files, activity per section, tags, policies, PUBLIC, admin holders, dormant users); the app never runs them. Names from the link are kept on one line with backslashes and quotes escaped (one_line, quoted, lit), so no name can start a statement of its own. See logic/page-sql.md.

name: Long tables are paged on the server
summary: window(p, key, n): slice(offset, offset+limit) from key= and limit= (PAGE by default, 0 = every row for CSV), offset reset past the end: Object users (m_offset), Sensitive objects / readers (o_offset, r_offset), What changed events (offset) (server.py:2422, 3348-3348, 3192). paged(p, rows): offset= / limit= (PAGE, at most 1000) for privs, access, held, grantees (server.py:1456-1460). Risks & fixes: FINDINGS_PAGE 100 (limit up to 500), counts and groups over every finding, one finding's fix via /api/finding?id= (server.py:3395, 3506, 3544). Review: REVIEW_PAGE 50 (limit up to 1000) (server.py:3706, 3770).

name: Independent reads run side by side
summary: each(): light SHOW waves SHOW_THREADS (16) at a time, heavy reads WORKERS (3) at a time on the one connection; answers in order, a failure as its exception, so one unreadable role skips only itself. SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT: SHOW / fallback statements as async child jobs BATCH (16) at a time (many), heavy INSERTs at most WORKERS at once (later / wait), async off for the run when its probe fails (async_o

name: Count paths without listing
summary: Exact counts over the role graph

name: Previous snapshot as .prev.pkl
summary: Replaced file of another run kept for What changed

name: A load says what it is doing

name: Each source: ACCOUNT_USAGE first, then INFORMATION_SCHEMA or SHOW
summary: live(): every ACCOUNT_USAGE view probed in one wave; a refused probe gives the fallback reason in the load log (access.py:1274-1288). Grants and user roles: ACCOUNT_USAGE, else SHOW ROLES / SHOW GRANTS TO|OF ROLE (access.py:1381-1435); users: ACCOUNT_USAGE, else SHOW USERS (access.py:1466-1488); query history: ACCOUNT_USAGE (30 days), else INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY over 7 windows of 167 h (week(), access.py:795-812, 1490-1503); tags and policies: ACCOUNT_USAGE, else INFORMATION_SCHEMA per table up to TAG_FALLBACK_MAX (access.py:1523-1559); database list, schema list and object inventory: ACCOUNT_USAGE, then INFORMATION_SCHEMA, then SHOW (business_rule:list_fallback_order, business_rule:inventory_levels); none readable -> UNAVAILABLE + note. mine(): ACCOUNT_USAGE grants / roles / user in one wave, SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE only when GRANTS_TO_ROLES fails (access.py:841-873). SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT AUTO does the same (fallback(), grants(), users(), usage(); sql/1_setup.sql:345-357, 380-455, 503-528, 530-561).

name: Every Snowflake read kept as a part; a load resumes
summary: Stage 1 keeps each read (heavy ACCOUNT_USAGE read, SHOW wave, snapshot table) as .cache/reads/<key>/<label>-<hash>.parquet, written by pyarrow, else duckdb (neither: no parts, a load reads everything; cache.py:370-378); the next load reads only the missing parts and, in a wave, only its timed-out statements; a part of a lost session is never kept; prune() drops parts a whole load did not ask for; the last OK snapshot run is always asked, never answered from a part (the answer is kept for --build); parts are read again only on Rebuild snapshot / Read Snowflake again or run.py --export --fresh; stage 2 needs no Snowflake

name: Risk strip of an object
summary: object_risks_of(o), from the grants without the Who has access walk: sensitive columns without masking while someone can read it; granted to PUBLIC (bad when sensitive); people (not service users) who can change a sensitive object; disabled or dormant readers; rule findings naming it; only admin roles reach it; not used in UNUSED (90) days yet at least WIDE (3) users can read it. Readers through READ_PRIVS, writers through WRITES, without users lacking USAGE on its database or schema (server.py:1838-1878).

name: Risk strip of a person or role
summary: risks_of(name, user), cached per subject: is an admin role; holds admin roles (shortest path per role); account privileges not from PUBLIC; reads sensitive objects unmasked; the rule findings (count per severity, first RISK_TOP 3 short rule names); default role is an admin role; dormant / disabled / never logged in and still holds roles; very broad access (reads >= BROAD 25% and >= BROAD_MIN 20 of the account's data objects); secondary roles ALL with more than one role. Each line: severity bad | warn, text, count, link, table; bad first (server.py:1724-1831). Lists name the first 3 then +N (more()). The unmasked-objects line links to What they see > Column by column, account privileges to Access > Can run.

name: A risk line opens its items in place
summary: A risk line with items carries table {cols, rows, total}: the first RISK_ROWS (10) rows; the strip opens it under the line, one at a time, and +N more or Open all goes to the page with all of them (server.py:1733-1739, web/src/components/kit.tsx:175-209). Lines without items (PUBLIC grants, admin role, broad access, ...) have table null.

summary: admin, database, FUNC prefix, TECH prefix, object, else group

summary: OWNERSHIP on a role is a privilege, not a link

name: Rule 1: Technical role granted to a user or group role
summary: Technical role granted to a user or group role. Why: Technical roles belong under functional roles only. Severity Medium (access.py:180).

name: Rule 10: Person can write to a sensitive object
summary: Person can write to a sensitive object. Why: Writes to sensitive data should come from the build or a service user. Severity Medium (access.py:181).

name: Rule 11: Sensitive object reachable through a group role
summary: Sensitive object reachable through a group role. Why: Group membership is managed outside Snowflake, so reviews miss it. Severity Low (access.py:181).

name: Rule 12: Admin role is a user's default role
summary: Admin role is a user's default role. Why: Every session starts with admin rights. Severity High (access.py:181).

name: Rule 13: Orphan role: no users and no parent roles
summary: Orphan role: no users and no parent roles. Why: Unused roles hide access that nobody reviews. Severity Low (access.py:181).

name: Rule 14: f'Chain deeper than {MAX_DEPTH_RULE} roles'
summary: f'Chain deeper than {MAX_DEPTH_RULE} roles'. Why: Long chains are hard to review and hide where access comes from. Severity Low (access.py:181).

name: Rule 15: Future grant in a schema that holds sensitive data
summary: Future grant in a schema that holds sensitive data. Why: New tables there are readable before anyone classifies them. Severity Medium (access.py:181).

name: Rule 16: f'Dormant user (no login for {DORMANT_DAYS} days) still holds roles'
summary: f'Dormant user (no login for {DORMANT_DAYS} days) still holds roles'. Why: Unused accounts are an easy way in. Severity Medium (access.py:182).

name: Rule 17: Read-only role can write
summary: Read-only role can write. Why: The role name or its use says read-only, but it can change data. Severity High (access.py:182).

name: Rule 18: Unusual privilege set
summary: Unusual privilege set. Why: The role holds more or fewer privileges than its capability (READ, WRITE, ...) stands for, so its name no longer tells what it can do. Severity Low (access.py:182).

name: Rule 19: EXECUTE TASK held by a person or consumer role
summary: EXECUTE TASK held by a person or consumer role. Why: Running tasks belongs to the build or a service user. Severity Medium (access.py:182).

name: Rule 2: Direct privilege on a functional role
summary: Direct privilege on a functional role. Why: Privileges sit on technical roles, so the role model stays reviewable. Severity Medium (access.py:180).

name: Rule 20: OPERATE on a task outside owner/build roles
summary: OPERATE on a task outside owner/build roles. Why: The task runs with its owner's privileges, so whoever can start or resume it borrows them. Severity High (access.py:182).

name: Rule 21: Warehouse MODIFY or OPERATE outside owner/build roles
summary: Warehouse MODIFY or OPERATE outside owner/build roles. Why: Resizing, suspending or resuming a warehouse changes cost and availability for everyone. Severity Medium (access.py:182).

name: Rule 22: Stream on sensitive table readable without the table
summary: Stream on sensitive table readable without the table. Why: A stream returns the table's changed rows, so it leaks data its reader cannot read in the table. Severity High (access.py:182).

name: Rule 23: CREATE privilege on a schema held by a read-only role
summary: CREATE privilege on a schema held by a read-only role. Why: A read-only role that can create objects can copy data or change the schema. Severity High (access.py:183).

name: Rule 24: Person changed data or a table's definition
summary: Medium. A person (in USER, not a service user) ran WRITE or DDL on a known object with a role that has no OWNERSHIP reach on it (data_use(role)[1][object] lacks "own"); one finding per user and object: statement counts, the most used role, last day. access.py:7632-7642

name: Rule 25: Service user used from an interactive client
summary: High. A service user (is_service) has activity rows whose CLIENT is in INTERACTIVE (Snowflake UI, SnowSQL, Snowflake CLI); one finding per service user: queries per client label, tables, last day. access.py:7627-7628, 7656-7662

name: Rule 26: Admin role used to read or change data
summary: High. Activity rows whose ROLE_NAME is in ADMIN on a known object; one finding per user and admin role: objects read, objects changed (action not READ), first three names. access.py:7629-7630, 7663-7667

name: Rule 27: First access to a table in the last 7 days
summary: Low. Per user and object: the first day on the object is within the last NEW_DAYS (7) days of the snapshot and the user had activity before cut - NEW_DAYS (not a new user); detail adds "sensitive" for tagged objects. access.py:7621, 7643-7647

name: Rule 28: Unusual volume on a table
summary: Medium. Per user and object with at least 5 active days: the busiest day has >= SPIKE[1] (50) queries and more than SPIKE[0] (3) x the median day. access.py:7648-7655

name: Rule 29: Streamlit app shows its owner's sensitive data to people who cannot read it
summary: High. Per Streamlit app (kinds STREAMLIT) whose owner roles (OWNERSHIP) read sensitive objects, per role holding USAGE on the app: users reaching that role who cannot read some of those objects through their own roles (user_reads) -> one finding on the holder role: app, owner, sensitive objects, users. Fix: revoke the app's USAGE from the role. access.py:6508-6523, app_exposure access.py:6468-6481

name: Rule 3: READ held directly and through another role
summary: READ held directly and through another role. Why: The direct grant is redundant and survives when the other one is removed. Severity Low (access.py:180).

name: Rule 4: OWNER role held by a consumer
summary: OWNER role held by a consumer. Why: Owners can drop and re-grant objects; only the build identity should own. Severity High (access.py:180).

name: Rule 5: Admin role held by a person
summary: Admin role held by a person. Why: Admin roles bypass the role model; use them through break-glass only. Severity High (access.py:180).

name: Rule 6: Sensitive column without a masking policy
summary: Sensitive column without a masking policy. Why: Everyone who can read the object sees the value in clear. Severity Medium (access.py:180).

name: Rule 7: Dormant or disabled person can read sensitive data
summary: Dormant or disabled person can read sensitive data. Why: Unused access to sensitive data is pure risk. Severity Critical (access.py:180).

name: Rule 8: Disabled user still holds roles
summary: Disabled user still holds roles. Why: Re-enabling the user brings all access back at once. Severity Low (access.py:180).

name: Rule 9: Privilege granted to PUBLIC
summary: Privilege granted to PUBLIC. Why: Every user, present and future, gets it. Severity High (access.py:181).

name: A rule group counts every person affected
summary: rule_index keeps every loser of a finding (not the first 50), so a group on Risks & fixes counts each person its findings affect once (server.py:3408).

name: Rules 17 and 23 walk only roles they can flag
summary: read_shares() counts per role the data objects reached, read only, written / owned, owned and schema CREATE grants; readonly_writes and rule23 skip a role neither the name nor the behaviour heuristic can flag before walking it

name: Server is the only SQL writer
summary: with_sql adds sql, roleDb, toDb to Compare / Request / Granted vs used changes; codegen.sqlOf only joins them

name: SESSIONS read only from a week before the first day
summary: activity_sql (and the same text in SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT) joins ACCOUNT_USAGE.SESSIONS created from 7 days before the first day read, not a year of sessions; a session open longer shows no client, so rule 25 may miss it

name: One ACCESS_HISTORY read for object use and activity
summary: history_sql scans ACCESS_HISTORY once (A0, from the earlier cut) for both; each part keeps its own cut; PART = USE / ACT rows split by history_rows (Direct mode) or one INSERT ALL in SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT history(). If the shared read fails, each step reads alone (one failing read fails only its step); not after a timeout (a read apart scans the same rows under the same limit)

name: Same snapshot run: nothing read again
summary: snapshot(old=cache.last): when the last OK RUN_ID equals the held data's and that data has the current shape (every table a list, no RUN_ID column, HOURS parsed), it is returned after the one TBL_ACCESS_RUN query; a new run reads every table again (test_server.test_same_run)

name: Every statement has a time limit that says how to raise it
summary: STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS as a statement parameter, not ALTER SESSION (the same locally and inside Snowflake); none on the SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT CALL (a cut CALL would leave its run RUNNING). A timeout (error 000630, access.timed_out) raises TimeoutError '<step>: stopped after 5 min (STATEMENT_TIMEOUT=300); set STATEMENT_TIMEOUT=600 for 10 minutes', or says a lower warehouse / account limit stoppe

name: Streams: ACCOUNT_USAGE.STREAMS, else SHOW
summary: Direct mode reads ACCOUNT_USAGE.STREAMS (one query, DELETED IS NULL) when grants came from ACCOUNT_USAGE, else SHOW STREAMS IN ACCOUNT, with a note that SHOW lists only the streams this role sees (access.py:987-988, 1627-1640). SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT streams(): the same order, SHOW when P_SOURCE = SHOW; an error leaves the source UNAVAILABLE and the run OK (sql/1_setup.sql:695-715).

name: A timeout means busy, not unreadable
summary: slow(e) = TimeoutError or error 000630 (timed_out). A probe that timed out counts as readable, so the full read is tried, not the SHOW fallback (access.py:1282-1284; sql/1_setup.sql:355-356). A full ACCOUNT_USAGE read that timed out: Direct mode notes the source UNAVAILABLE (SHOW would be slower still) (access.py:1389-1390, 1473-1474); SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT fails the run instead (sql/1_setup.sql:403-404, 514-515). Refused (any other error) -> the fallback. A timed-out part is kept as failed and read again on the next load (cache.py:492, 510); a refresh with timed-out reads keeps the old data (server.py:4215-4218).

name: One spelling per object type
summary: spell(kind): underscores become spaces (GRANTS_TO_ROLES says EXTERNAL_TABLE, SHOW says EXTERNAL TABLE); role links (ROLE, DATABASE_ROLE, APPLICATION_ROLE) and non-text keep theirs. tidy() respells GRANTED_ON of every TBL_ACCESS_GRANT row, so older snapshots and Direct mode match (access.py:1983-1984); SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT has the same spell() and writes the inventory's OWNERSHIP rows with it (sql/1_setup.sql:313-314, 963).

name: A person or role
summary: page=access: A person or role: tabs Overview (risk strip, why) / Objects (heat per database and schema, list) / Privileges / Paths / Can run / Activity / History; a role also Held by, What it holds, All protected, Read-only writes (roleTabs, from /api/role); one page of objects at their highest level, filtered by access, type and heat cell, paged on the server, CSV of every entry from /api/access.csv

name: Access graph
summary: page=graph: Access graph from a table, role or person; tabs Hierarchy / Trace; filters database or schema (ScopePick), object type, access; a click shows only the lines through a box (focus=), its detail beside the graph, the line legend under it; the map is fetched only on the Trace tab, a box opened later asks map node=

name: Activity tab
summary: Tab on the Object and Access pages: one access log of stacked sections (CLAUDE.md exception to tabs): lead and source line, tiles or app viewers, off-hours, who touched what heat grid, hours of use with business-time slider, objects in detail, who used, sensitive, paths, DDL, copy-only SQL, checks

name: Can they?
summary: page=check: Can they?: verdict Yes / Partly / No / Blocked with USAGE chips and risk strip; tabs Inside (a database or schema, first then) / Answer (why blocked, graph) / Routes (Routes, Where to cut, Table) / Ways in (No: the narrowest grant first, owning apart) / Rows & columns (layers, what they see); any privilege Snowflake has on the type can be asked, USAGE on a table asks its database and schema

name: Catalog
summary: Sensitive objects catalog (screen 8), most exposed first

name: Compare
summary: page=compare: Compare two people or roles: overlap circles, the sentence, Make B equal to A; tabs Differences (only A / only B / different / same) / Plan (tab=plan: Make B equal to A, Give B what A has, Remove what only A has; only with something to plan; revokes simulated on What if)

name: Granted vs used
summary: page=usage: Granted vs used (ACCESS_HISTORY): weekly queries, All / Not used / Partly used / Keep / Sensitive tabs, unused grants on the trim tab

name: Home
summary: page=home: Home: hero search (Find, "can X read Y") with the question links, recently viewed (first 3), then tabs Risks (Needs attention tiles, act-first, risk cards, By area folded) / At a glance (the account, Object activity card) / Changes (What changed)

name: Object activity
summary: page=objuse: Object activity (shared only): every table, view, warehouse and Streamlit app by last use; tabs Not used / Read, never written / Written, never read / All objects; days 30 / 90 / 180, type and scope filters; server-paged table and CSV

name: Plan
summary: Change plan tab (screen 11) shared with Risks & fixes

name: Request access
summary: page=request: Request access: suggested roles (the 3 smallest, then +N more), approver, SQL/Terraform/ticket text

name: Review & sign-off
summary: page=review: Review & sign-off: review grid tab first; (user, object) rows paged, filtered and sorted on the server with part tabs in the side menu, CSV of every row

name: ReviewGrid
summary: Review grid (screen 6): people x objects, scope tabs in the side menu (up to 8), Keep/Revoke, sign-off CSV

name: Risks
summary: Change plan tab (RisksTab), HeatGrid, PlanPanel, RuleList used by Risks & fixes

name: Risks & fixes
summary: page=rules: Risks & fixes: tabs Findings / Change plan / Admin holders / Dormant & disabled / Rules; counts and groups from the server (by rule / person / object / grid), one group's findings fetched when opened as aligned rows (who, what, users losing access with names behind the count, Fix), fix texts from /api/finding; severities and rules in the side menu under Findings

name: Role paths
summary: page=role (not in the side menu unless open): Role paths: risk strip, tabs Diagram (KPIs, in scope when a scope is set) / Privileges (/api/privs of=role) / Held by (paged by /api/held) / What it holds (one type at a time) / All protected / Read-only writes; inside Access one part (pane) without its own tabs and strip

name: Sensitive data
summary: page=sensitive: Sensitive data: a line of counts, tagged objects and readers as server-paged tables, masked columns, who can read; Catalog tab

name: Sensitive data flow
summary: page=flow: Sensitive data flow: people -> granted role -> sensitive object; tabs Objects / Roles / Graph; the selected box's first 5 people, all as CSV (/api/flow.csv)

name: User paths
summary: page=user (not in the side menu unless open): User paths: tabs Diagram / Privileges (each tab paged by /api/privs, its diagram from /api/graph?of=user-tab) / Reached more than one way / All protected / Sensitive reach / Role usage; findings on top

name: What changed
summary: page=changes: What changed between this and the previous snapshot (compared at refresh time), events paged on the server, filter tabs (All / Gained access / ...) in the side menu; watched questions

name: What if
summary: page=whatif: What if: simulated revokes, tabs Impact (Who loses / Objects / Roles / Findings / Text to apply) / Plan, CSV in the head, IaC/REVOKE text (never run); changing the role keeps the picked user or role, Add only when they hold it

name: What they see
summary: page=see: What they see: risk strip (quiet), tabs Column by column (default) / All protected / Sensitive reach / Role usage; old part= links still open their tab

name: What changed
